subject: GPU capacity selection & burst policy for Synthetix Health - next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@synthetix.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU capacity selection & burst policy for Synthetix Health - next steps

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We captured the high-level intake and I wanted to propose a concrete path forward so CS/Ops have a single ownerable checklist to run with. Quick summary:

- Target launch: pilot traffic (prod-read) in Q1 pre-prod window; initial pool in us-west-2, with on-demand burst into us-east-1 as a fallback.
- Steady state need: ~12 concurrent 8k-context streams (~2x peak headroom).
- Burst model: short bursts up to 2x baseline for scheduled events, with warm-warm start (pre-warm for predicted windows).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Synthetix to confirm egress/data residency constraints (are there any PHI routing locks to keep in a specific region?).
2) Redwood Ops (Markus + Logan) to validate capacity availability and suggest pool sizing and warm-start policy.
3) Procurement to sign commitment for reserved capacity or agree on a hybrid reserved + burst pricing model.

I've attached a lightweight selection matrix and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) that maps owners and dates. Can you confirm the residency callouts and approve a 2-week window for an operations readiness review?

Thanks —
Tessa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Hi Tessa —

Thanks, that reads well. A few clarifications from our side:
- Data residency: for now PHI must remain in us-west-2 for initial rollout. We can consider us-east-1 for non-PHI workloads later.
- Procurement: procurement copied for the billing/commit question — we are open to a 6-month reserved minimum + burst at usage-based pricing.
- Bursting: we prefer warm-start (short-lived pre-warm) rather than full reserved extra capacity due to cost.

We're good to do the ops readiness review the week of 11/9 — does that work for your team? Also, Claire here is primary for technical sign-off; procurement will handle contracts.

Best,
Claire Zhao
Head of Platform Engineering
Synthetix Health

Subject: Fwd: GPU capacity selection & burst policy for Synthetix Health - ops readiness week of 11/9?

Markus / Logan —

Looping you in to scope the readiness review. Claire confirmed PHI must remain in us-west-2 for initial rollout and they prefer warm-start bursting rather than large reserved overprovision. Key asks for the readiness review:

- Validate pool topology in us-west-2 for 12 concurrent 8k streams with 2x headroom and estimated token throughput (p50/p95).
- Define warm-start window and warm cache strategy (KV cache priming, prefix cache policy).
- Confirm netops requirements for egress ACLs and cross-region fallback to us-east-1 for non-PHI (if we enable).
- Draft escalation path if warm-start fails (fallback model: degrade to smaller model variant or queue).

I've attached the MAP and matrix. Please add a short readiness checklist itemizing who will run which tests during the 11/9 review.

Tessa

[Attachment: MAP_Synthetix_v0.3.docx (docx)]
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@synthetix.health>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: GPU capacity selection & burst policy for Synthetix Health - ops readiness week of 11/9?

Thanks for the context. Quick operational plan and timeline:

1) Capacity validation (by 11/4): we will run a sizing sim with a 8k-token average payload and your stated concurrency to estimate p50/p95 latency and GPU unit-hours. Expect a short report (1 page) with recommended pool size and a recommended quantization profile.

2) Warm-start policy (by 11/6): propose a pre-warm window of 10 minutes for scheduled bursts plus a predictive pre-warm hook we can trigger via API from Synthetix. For spontaneous spikes we recommend a 2-step fallback: a) fast fallback to a smaller 4k model variant for 60s, b) then spin up additional warm nodes. We'll include KV cache priming recommendations and a sample cache key list for initial priming.

3) Netops coordination (by 11/4): Logan will validate egress ACLs; notes: PHI-only traffic must have no cross-region egress; for non-PHI we will test cross-region failover to us-east-1 in a lab environment (no PHI).

4) Ops readiness session (11/9 10:00-11:30 PT): agenda will include sim results, warm-start demo, netops checklist, and a go/no-go checklist. We will provide a runbook artifact and a short on-call rotation for the first 72 hours post-launch.

I attached an initial checklist snippet in-line below and will push the full runbook to the shared drive.

[Checklist excerpt]
- Validate reserved pool GPU type (A10G vs A100 cost/latency tradeoff)
- Confirm autoscale policy thresholds (queue length, average latency)
- KV cache priming script and sample prefixes
- Warm-start API trigger and TTL semantics
- Fallback model mapping and circuit-breaker thresholds

Markus
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the plan looks good. Confirming:
- We will keep PHI in us-west-2 for pilot.
- We agree to a 6-month reserved minimum for an A10G-based pool + warm-bursting as described; procurement will follow up with a PO and contract redlines.
- 11/9 10:00 PT works for the ops readiness review — Claire + a platform engineer will attend.

Please include the runbook link in the calendar invite and a short pre-read (2 pages) on the sizing sim. We'll sign the MAP after procurement confirms the PO.
